title: Overview | Charts | Data visualization | Visa Product Design System

blocks.t: Explore chart components and best practices for visualizing and communicating data insights.
Explore our collection of chart examples, which have been tailored to support Visa’s most common business scenarios and analysis tasks.
Bar chart used to compare differences between categories, such as countries or product types.
Bar chart used to compare trends to a threshold such as goal, budget or average.
Bar chart used to summarize the range of values of a distribution and identify the most common values.
Bar chart used to summarize and compare trends.
Bar chart used to identify high and low values and comparing trends.
Dumbbell plot used to identify over or underperforming categories relative to a benchmark.
Dumbbell plot used to compare variance and pace of growth between two date periods.
Heatmap used to compare categories across discrete date parts.
Dumbbell plot used to compare variance between two categories over time.
Heatmap used to highlight one category's contribution to the total, and compare values to a threshold.
Heatmap used to compare two metrics, and identify the most and least common combinations.
Heatmap used to visualize a metric in a calendar format, to identify seasonal peak.
Line chart used to compare trends to a threshold such as goal, budget or average.
Line chart used to compare a primary metric to a secondary metric, such as current to previous year.
Line chart used to compare differences in trends between multiple categories, with emphasis on a primary category.
Line chart used to compare differences in trends between two to five categories.
